title: Evil
body: I’m shocked. I’ve spent hundreds of dollars on manga, and I’ve slowly downloaded my files for offline viewing, and arranged into my bookshelf collection. Now out of nowhere, all my downloads are forcibly deleted, and I’m forced to a new app. And every file must be downloaded one by one again. I don’t even see a bulk download feature. You cannot trust this company with your money. They have shown they will remove your content and there’s nothing you can do about it. Edit: even worse, I downloaded my manga on this app. After a month break of using the app I come back and I’m signed out and all downloads gone. What’s wrong with these guys? I bought the manga, it’s not a rental, so why is it being deleted so aggressively? I will never buy another manga from these guys again. Edit 2: The developers response is misleading. The problem is I have a lot of manga, and I download for offline use such as on the subway. This app has deleted my downloaded manga from my phone. I have purchased the manga, so the app should not be aggressively signing me out and deleting my downloaded titles without any warning. Edit 3: I understand there was a migration. I’m over that already. There is now a different, new problem. After I downloaded my hundreds of manga on the new app, they were deleted all again. I did not use the app for about two weeks, and when I opened it up I was signed out and all downloaded content was deleted. This is not a subscription, so there is no explanation for why all my offline content is removed if I have not opened the app recently. I should not be automatically signed out and content removed. If I download content in the new app it should stay downloaded. The is the new app, and recently downloaded files. In this new app, downloaded content is being deleted. If I download all my content, then two weeks later open the app on the subway, and I’m only greeted with a sign in page and no content that’s terrible. Why should I spend more money on manga here, when the hundreds of dollars already spent can’t stay on my phone.

title: Just let us use the old version
body: You know it’s bad when you get spammed with ads and offers while just trying to sign in. The previous app had a much more elegant form of integration with the store in the app: one tab for the store and that’s it, and you can search from there. I do not wish my Library to be cordoned off to a small section of the app so the store takes the main stage. Worse yet the store makes you buy “coins” which you can use the then buy books. This is a common way to obfuscate purchases and incentivizes consumers to spend more money. In the old version, the coins earned from purchases were a simple way to receive discounts for repeat buyers. The former traps your purchases behind pseudo-currency, the other thanks you for patronage. The new “Library” is featureless! No sorting, no Bookshelves, no charm. Even the new logo looks minimalist and lifeless. You’re telling me I have to use search filters to find my audiobooks? Fire the developers who made this version, fire the people who made the new storefront, and just let us use the old one. The other version was not broken and did NOT need fixing. The Chinese port of this app was a copy of all that was good in the original Japanese version. Tell me why English readers get screwed over with the least consumer friendly version of this service. I wanted an app to read my downloaded books, an E-Reader not a toxic storefront. And before these “developers “ try to argue that they are working on improving the app; no they are not. This app is just corporate greed puppeting the corpse of a once great service. We all know that there is no going back, and soon they intend to wipe our English purchases from the old app, forcing us to use this dumpster fire of an app. I got an email today saying such. You couldn’t even let those who prefer a better experience use the legacy version. Consumer protection is not real in the western world, and this shows.

title: Disappointing Refresh
body: Truthfully if I was allowed to give 0 stars I would. As a loyal customer for over four years, this new app feels like not only a huge step backwards, but also a spit in the face of loyal customers. The migration of my account to the new system went smoothly, which is one of the few good things I can say after my first day of use. Basic features do not even work at launch, or are completely missing. I migrated 929 titles from the old system, and text search within the library does not work. I can type a title exactly and get 0 results. With a library as large as I have, this is incredibly inconvenient. On top of that, filtering that used to exist no longer does. You can no longer filter by reading status (i.e. "unread"), and you can no longer filter by download status either. You can't even mark titles as read anymore, so there is no reliable way to track what you haven't read yet. There is a new "History" tab under the "Library" section, but this only shows titles you've opened. The "History" tab and other tabs in the "Library" are only visible when you are at the top, so if you're 200 titles in to a 929 title library, there's a lot of scrolling back up to the top to switch tabs. Bookmarking is also seemingly missing, or located in an unintuitive spot in the UI. As a reading app this is a baffling omission. The bookshelf feature was completely cut from the new app. This was my most used feature of the old app as it allowed me to organize my unread books into the order that I wanted to read them in. With the lack of even being able to filter for unread titles in my library, there is no conceivable way for me to keep track of my library within the app I purchased these books in anymore, which is beyond disappointing. You also can no longer load third party EPUB or PDF files into the app. While this feature was buried in a somewhat inconvenient location in the old app, at least it was supported. The notification system also appears to be completely gone. I found this incredibly convenient in the old app and website as it was a quick place to check for new pre-orders for series I've been reading or seeing current sales/promotions. I am looking forward to seeing how the new site addresses this. Overall I have found two silver linings: 1. The new website allows you to download your purchases. These are DRM protected files, but as a consumer there's now the power to choose what app to read your purchases in at the cost of having to put in a password (your user ID found on the website) to unlock the book when you start reading. 2. My English titles have not disappeared from the old app that's intended to be for Japanese titles only going forward. This means that I can continue reading off of my curated reading list there for the immediate future. I will be leveraging #2 while I work my way through #1 downloading and backing up my entire library so I can decide how I want to move forward with organizing my library. I will now be spending a decent chuck of my weekend I had planned to spend reading books taking care of this instead. As of today, the coin system provides a somewhat compelling reason to continue purchasing books through Bookwalker as a platform, but I have found exactly 0 compelling reasons to continue trying to use the new app until basic and organizational features found in the old app are added back. I truly hope someone from Bookwalker reads this and their team can work to make fixes and improvements over the coming months to save this app that's essentially dead on release.

title: It’s okay
body: I wouldn’t continue using the app in its current state, almost every time I go to a new chapter it starts on the second to last page so I kept having to either scroll up or back to the last chapter then forward to get to the first page.

title: Downgrade from original
body: A complete downgrade from the original app. I have over a hundred books in my library and none of them are sorted. Old app sorted by alphabet, and grouped series together. Now its just a messy bookshelf. Also the only way to view downloaded books is by going offline. Old app downloaded books in order to read them but you could still view your collection even if they weren’t downloaded. There is also no more bookmark feature. Finally, if you were in middle of reading a book on the old app, just opening up the app automatically took you to where you left off. In the new app you have to manually go to your library and find the book in order to resume reading. The app is alright, but at the moment it is so much worse than the old app. Please work on this!

title: I dunno
body: I wish there was a free option with ads and then a payed option without ads. I wasn’t planing to use money on online manga I was hoping you could just watch it with ads- so I would appreciate the choice of doing an ads version just not way too many ads.

title: Major downgrade
body: The previous app was better in almost every way. We can’t make bookshelves to organize our collections into groups, we can’t archive books we no longer wish to see, we can’t delete books from our library we no longer want. Used to love the comfy feel of the old app. The new minimalist setup feels like a major downgrade from what was. I wish I could immigrate my collection and go back to the previous app.

title: The old app was better
body: No offline reading. No bookshelves. The sorting system isn’t it good. The search system doesn’t work. Reading light novels images is hard, they are so tiny.

title: A huge downgrade
body: I usually don’t write reviews on apps, but this is quite bad. We lose the ability to organize our libraries. We also lose the ability to download books, so if you want to read somewhere with no internet your out of luck. We do get the ability to buy books using the app, but only with coins that hide the real price. This is a huge downgrade to the original app.

title: Still room to improve

title: Interface is different
body: Haven’t read in a year and I come back to find ownership has separated from JP and there’s a new website and new app. I liked the simple UI of the old app. I miss the “read/unread” visual aid. And in place of the old “ xx% read” visual aid they put a small bar to give you an idea your progress but I like the exact number better than the bar. You can kind of create bookshelves like before but now they’re called “collections”. It’s not as visually appealing as the bookshelves because it just shows the books there in a row but I guess it works. I just miss how comfy the bookshelves felt. I’m still just starting to use the app and UI so I will come back and update this review as I continue to get familiar with it. I heard you can’t offline read anymore so I will be checking that next.

title: Its ok…

title: Bad to Moderately Acceptable
body: Overall worse experience than previous app 1. Cannot read books without internet connection 2. Cannot organize purchased collection by series 3. Cannot see un-purchased sequels to partially owned series 4. Images in light novels don’t scale properly and cannot be properly viewed Same applies to the web version as well. How exactly does this “serve us better” ? ————- Adding to previous review: 6/26/26 Updates have so far restored ~60-70% of the functionality of the previous app (now Japan store only). Sorting your collection by series is now possible, downloads for offline are possible, image scaling seems mostly fine now. The UI isn’t awesome, but the bones are there for tweaking to make it better. Most menus require too many taps on a touch screen to access comfortably. Biggest issue: no way to see easily see what un-purchased titles are available or soon to be released for series you own. It’s possible to see it from a particular series’s store page, but that’s slow to navigate two. On the previous store you could tell at a glance that a series had a newly released volume available. Thus I miss that there are new volumes and don’t spend money on them.

title: Great reading experience, But please add a library or bookshelf, organizational feature
body: I have been a long-time user of the original BookWalker app, and I’m happy to say that after switching to the new app, All of the books I’ve purchased transferred over and I haven’t had any issues reading them. However, I’ve been purchasing manga through BookWalker for years and have built a very large collection. One feature I loved about the original app was the ability to organize books into custom bookshelves and arrange my library however I wanted. With the new app, there doesn’t seem to be a way to organize your collection, and if you have a large library like I do, it can be difficult to navigate all of your purchased books. This app would be a 10/10 for me if it added a digital bookshelf feature that allowed users to organize their purchased books in whatever way works best for them.

title: Over all Fine. One issue I cannot over look
body: Over all the new app is fine and the think the good and bad even each over out in the broad strokes. The good: - it does not take multiple attempts to open the app like the old app sometimes took -when you have a book open you can click the title to see the other books in the series and open them from there - seems to load faster than the old app alert from the first time you open a book The bad: - no bookshelf or equivalent in the new app - opens to the store instead of your library, makes a worse user experience as it feels like a storefront first and not an e-reader, the storefront and obnoxious adds should be left for the website Now this is the one problem that I really cannot overlook, the issues with downloading books. As I’ll be at sea for extended period of time with limited internet I like to download media and barriers to this make ethical consumption all the more difficult and is what drives many to turn to piracy. That said the issue I am having is that when I select a title and choose to download if sometimes it will get the “Download scheduled” tag and then never download eve after other things are done downloading, sometimes I can just cancel the scheduled download then redo it and it works then but the real bug is that for a some titles it gets stuck with that scheduled download and I cannot even cancel it.

title: Needs work
body: The color definitely does look better and easier on the eyes in the new app. I would like to have the old sorting system back so I have have my books listed by title and have to click on it to show the volume or chapters. Also an easier method to download the books would should also added to the new app similar to the old one where I can select multiple titles with ease instead of holding then allowing a single download. If it’s possible please include a method to minimize or change the font or format size of the books because right now it’s about 3 books per swipe down and since I have multiple titles it’ll be very difficult to find or scroll through what I want. Also the favorites section doesn’t help me too much since it’s just books I put on wish list. if it’s possible to include self made tabs or extra tabs similar to Gmail it would help a lot. Hopefully more updates and changes can be made to this new app and good luck to the team. Right now I’m going to stick with the older version 3 stars for now

title: It's fine. Not great, but not as bad as everyone is making it out to be.
body: At first I was a bit upset because, after migrating my account from Bookwalker Global, it seemed that none of my purchases transferred. I was able to find advice online that directed me to check my restricted content settings, and I found that Mature Content and images were off by default. After toggling them on, my prior purchases appeared were they should be. Overall, I wish it were easier to more accurately sort available titles, and I wish I could purchase japanese language content now that the original app is region-locked.

title: Great for Manga
body: It is really easy now to read manga. The filters for reading and unread still don’t work if you’re using the group view. Reading light novels still not great I already switched over to Apple Books for that since I read a lot on it anyways mostly because cross infinite worlds is no longer on this platform. Will start randomly at the end of the manga even if it’s a fresh purchase. Other than those mild flaws works great.

title: Ups and Downs
body: New app is mostly better, but still has some growing pains to work through. You’ll probably encounter any issues I’ve seen yourself, so I won’t spend a lot of time on that. What I will say: new app is faster on both old and new devices, has better reading options, and I love the way you can quickly flip through a book if needed. I find it weird that the arrows at the bottom move between volumes, but for certain shorter books this makes a lot of sense. Maybe make it configurable? Having the store be better integrated into the app is nice. That said, I’ll probably try to mainly purchase books from the website, since in app is a little more confusing. Makes sense though, with the cut that Apple takes, they have to do more to profit off the app sales. I’d recommend buying from the website anyway just to support the platform better, rather than giving Apple more pocket change. Excited to see where this app goes!
